question: Across CBA, NAB and Westpac in FY25, which bank best converted its disclosed underlying top-line or pre-provision performance into its preferred cash/core earnings measure, and what explains the ordering? Compare direction and drivers rather than absolute dollars, and state the comparability limits of the three non-identical profit measures.
answer:
**CBA converted best.** Its pre-provision "Operating performance" rose 3% and cash NPAT rose 4% — the only one of the three whose preferred cash/core measure grew faster than its pre-provision line. Westpac ranks second (pre-provision profit −3%, net profit ex Notable Items −2%, cushioned by a 21% fall in impairments); NAB ranks last (underlying profit +1.3% turned into cash earnings −0.2% after a 14.4% rise in credit impairment charges).

**Reasoning (each bank on its own printed basis):**
- **CBA** (FY ended 30 Jun 25, cash basis): total operating income +5% to $28,465m; total operating expenses +6% to $12,996m (investment spend $2,297m, +14%) held Operating performance to +3% ($15,469m); loan impairment expense fell 9% ($802m→$726m), "reflecting lower loss experience and improved economic conditions", lifting cash NPAT (continuing) +4% to $10,252m. NIM of 2.08% was +9bps headline but only +2bps excluding the mix effect of lower liquid assets and institutional pooled facilities.
- **WBC** (FY ended 30 Sep 25, ex Notable Items): net operating income +3% to $22,464m, but expenses +9% (including $273m Fit for Growth restructuring; +6% excluding it) drove pre-provision profit −3% to $10,548m; impairment charges fell 21% ($537m→$424m; 5bps vs 7bps of average gross loans), so net profit ex Notable Items fell only 2% to $6,972m.
- **NAB** (FY ended 30 Sep 25, cash basis): revenue +2.9% (M&T-driven; +1.4% ex-M&T) against expenses +4.6% (including $130m payroll review/remediation; +3.2% excluding) gave underlying profit +1.3% ($10,965m); the credit impairment charge rose 14.4% ($728m→$833m), pushing cash earnings −0.2% to $7,091m.

The ordering is set by impairment direction: CBA's falling impairments amplified positive pre-provision growth; WBC's falling impairments cushioned a negative pre-provision result; NAB's rising impairments consumed its positive pre-provision growth.

**Comparability limits:** the three measures are not identical. CBA's cash NPAT excludes only non-cash items (hedging/IFRS volatility and disposal losses; −$137m after tax in FY25) but keeps restructuring/notable items ($130m) inside expenses. NAB's cash earnings additionally adds back acquired-intangible amortisation ($49m) and acquisitions/integration/disposals ($451m) in FY25, and restated FY24 comparatives for an expense-presentation change. WBC's net profit ex Notable Items excluded only hedging items (−$56m post-tax; large items nil) in FY25 — WBC itself calls measures ex-NI "comparable to a 'cash earnings' basis" — and keeps the $273m restructuring in expenses. Year-ends differ (CBA June; NAB/WBC September), and all three are non-IFRS/non-AAS, unaudited management measures, so growth rates are compared on each bank's own basis, not a common one.

key_facts.fact: CBA FY25 (cash basis): Operating performance +3% to $15,469m and cash NPAT from continuing operations +4% to $10,252m — bottom line grew faster than pre-provision performance.
CBA loan impairment expense fell 9% ($802m to $726m), reflecting lower loss experience and improved economic conditions — the tailwind behind its conversion.
CBA total operating expenses rose 6% to $12,996m, with investment spend of $2,297m up 14%, capping Operating performance growth at 3% despite income +5%.
CBA NIM was 2.08%, +9bps on FY24 headline but only +2bps excluding the mix effect of lower liquid assets and institutional pooled facilities.
WBC FY25 (ex Notable Items): pre-provision profit fell 3% to $10,548m while net profit ex Notable Items fell only 2% to $6,972m.
WBC operating expenses rose 9% including $273m Fit for Growth restructuring costs; excluding these, expenses rose 6%.
WBC impairment charges fell 21% ($537m to $424m), from 7bps to 5bps of average gross loans, cushioning the bottom line.
NAB FY25 (cash basis): underlying profit rose 1.3% to $10,965m but cash earnings fell 0.2% to $7,091m — the only bank whose bottom line fell despite pre-provision growth.
NAB revenue rose 2.9% (1.4% ex-M&T) and expenses rose 4.6% including $130m payroll review and remediation charges (3.2% excluding).
NAB credit impairment charge rose 14.4% ($728m to $833m), consuming its underlying profit growth.
CBA cash basis excludes only non-cash items (−$137m after tax FY25) but keeps $130m restructuring/notable items inside expenses.
NAB cash earnings adds back $49m acquired-intangible amortisation and $451m acquisitions/integration/disposals in FY25, and restated FY24 comparatives for an expense-presentation change.
WBC net profit ex Notable Items is a non-AAS measure; FY25 Notable Items were only hedging items (−$56m post-tax), and WBC calls ex-NI measures comparable to a cash earnings basis.

limitations: The banks print no 'conversion' metric; the ranking is derived from each bank's own printed growth rates, which sit on non-identical measure definitions (CBA cash NPAT vs NAB cash earnings vs WBC net profit ex Notable Items).
Fiscal periods differ: CBA's FY ended 30 June 2025; NAB's and WBC's FY ended 30 September 2025 — a three-month timing difference in the rate and credit environment.
NAB restated FY24 comparatives for an expense-presentation change, so its growth rates are on a restated basis.
Bank-defined 'underlying' adjustments (CBA NIM +2bps ex-mix; NAB revenue +1.4% ex-M&T; WBC expenses +6% ex-restructuring) are each bank's own qualifications, not common adjustments.
Absolute dollars were not compared per the question; the three banks differ in scale (cash NPAT $10.3bn CBA vs $7.1bn NAB vs $7.0bn WBC), so equal percentage moves are unequal dollar amounts.
All three preferred measures are non-IFRS/non-AAS and unaudited; statutory results differ (e.g. CBA statutory NPAT $10,116m, NAB statutory net profit $6,759m, WBC statutory net profit $6,916m).
